answer.summary: Using the Freedman (1982) approximation for two-sided log-rank test with a hazard ratio of 0.7, event probabilities of 0.3707 (treatment) and 0.4890 (control), two-sided alpha=0.05, target power=0.80, and equal allocation (1:1), the required sample size is 294 participants per group (588 total). The continuous solution (293.17) was rounded up to the nearest integer following standard sample size convention.
answer.method: Freedman approximation (Freedman, 1982) implemented via powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default. The method calculates the required number of events using m = (1/k)·[(k·HR+1)/(HR-1)]²·(z₁₋α/₂+z₁₋β)², then converts to participant sample size using n = m·k/(k·pE+pC) and n = m/(k·pE+pC). Sample sizes are rounded up to integers.

Independent observations
Large-sample validity of central limit theorem approximation

Method assumes proportional hazards which may not hold in practice
Does not account for potential protocol violations, non-adherence, or irregular follow-up patterns
Sample size is deterministic under specified parameters; actual trial power may vary with realized event probabilities
No adjustment for multiple comparisons if planned

# Install and load powerSurvEpi for verification
if (!requireNamespace("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", quiet = TRUE)
}
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Define parameters
alpha <- 0.05  # two-sided significance level
power <- 0.80  # target power
hr <- 0.7      # hazard ratio (alternative)
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # event probability in treatment group
p_control <- 0.4890    # event probability in control group
allocation_ratio <- 1  # equal allocation

# Calculate using powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default
# This function uses Freedman approximation
# ssizeCT.default computes sample size per group for two-sample survival test

result <- ssizeCT.default(
  alpha = alpha,
  power = power,
  hazardRatio = hr,
  p1 = p_treatment,
  p2 = p_control
)

# Extract sample size per group
n_per_group_continuous <- result$n

# Standard ceiling rounding for sample size
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_per_group_continuous)

cat("=== Freedman Approximation for Log-Rank Test ===\n")
cat("Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (two-sided): %g\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power: %g\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  Hazard ratio: %g\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("  Event probability (treatment): %g\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("  Event probability (control): %g\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio: %g\n", allocation_ratio))
cat("\nResults:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Continuous sample size per group: %.4f\n", n_per_group_continuous))
cat(sprintf("  Integer sample size per group (ceiling): %d\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Total sample size: %d\n", 2 * n_per_group))

# Verification: compute power at the rounded sample size
# Use powerSurvEpi::powerSurvEpi for power verification
power_check <- powerSurvEpi(
  N = 2 * n_per_group,  # total sample size
  hazardRatio = hr,
  p1 = p_treatment,
  p2 = p_control,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat(sprintf("\nVerification - Achieved power at n=%d per group: %.6f\n", 
            n_per_group, power_check$power)

# Also check power at ceiling - 1
n_lower <- n_per_group - 1
if (n_lower > 0) {
  power_lower <- powerSurvEpi(
    N = 2 * n_lower,
    hazardRatio = hr,
    p1 = p_treatment,
    p2 = p_control,
    alpha = alpha
  )
  cat(sprintf("Power at n=%d per group: %.6f\n", n_lower, power_lower$power))
}

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_list <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_group, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = 2 * n_per_group, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_check$power, 6), unit = "proportion")
  )
)

cat("\n=== Output for Structured Reporting ===\n")
cat("Primary metric: sample_size = ", n_per_group, " participants_per_group\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", round(power_check$power, 6), "\n")

# Return as JSON
library(jsonlite)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(result_list, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

       k: numeric. ratio of participants in group E (experimental
          group) compared to group C (control group).

      pE: numeric. probability of failure in group E (experimental

      pC: numeric. probability of failure in group C (control group)

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the sample size calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the number of participants needed in each group to
     achieve a power of 1-beta is

           n_E=\frac{m k}{k p_E + p_C}, n_C=\frac{m}{k p_E + p_C}       
     
     where

     m=\frac{1}{k}<=ft(\frac{k RR + 1}{RR - 1}\right)^2<=ft(
     z_{1-alpha/2}+z_{1-beta}
     \right)^2,
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1).

     A two-element vector. The first element is n_E and the second
     element is n_C.

_ N_ o_ t_ e:

     (1) The sample size formula assumes that the central-limit theorem
     is valid and hence is appropriate for large samples. (2) n_E and
     n_C will be rounded up to integers.

# Verify the Freedman approximation manually
# Formula from the documentation:
# n_E = m*k / (k*pE + pC)
# n_C = m / (k*pE + pC)
# where m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta})^2

# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
power <- 0.80
beta <- 1 - power  # 0.20
hr <- 0.7  # This is RR in the formula (hazard ratio)
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # pE (experimental)
p_control <- 0.4890    # pC (control)
k <- 1  # allocation ratio

# Critical values from standard normal distribution
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # two-sided
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - beta)  # one-sided for power

cat("=== Manual Verification of Freedman Approximation ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Input parameters:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  alpha (two-sided): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  beta (1 - power): %.4f\n", beta))
cat(sprintf("  power: %.4f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  HR (RR): %.1f\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("  pE (treatment): %.4f\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("  pC (control): %.4f\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("  k (allocation ratio): %.1f\n\n", k))

cat(sprintf("Critical values:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  z_{1-alpha/2} (two-sided): %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_{1-beta} (power): %.6f\n\n", z_beta))

# Compute m using the formula
numerator_ratio <- (k * hr + 1) / (hr - 1)
cat(sprintf("Formula components:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  (k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1) = (%.1f*%.1f + 1)/(%.1f - 1) = %.6f\n", 
            k, hr, hr, numerator_ratio))

ratio_squared <- numerator_ratio^2
cat(sprintf("  Squared ratio: %.6f\n", ratio_squared))

z_sum <- z_alpha_2 + z_beta
z_sum_squared <- z_sum^2
cat(sprintf("  (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta})^2 = (%.6f + %.6f)^2 = %.6f\n\n",
            z_alpha_2, z_beta, z_sum_squared))

m <- (1/k) * ratio_squared * z_sum_squared
cat(sprintf("m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta})^2\n"))
cat(sprintf("m = (1/%.1f) * %.6f * %.6f\n", k, ratio_squared, z_sum_squared))
cat(sprintf("m = %.6f\n\n", m))

# Compute sample sizes
denominator <- k * p_treatment + p_control
cat(sprintf("Denominator: k*pE + pC = %.1f*%.4f + %.4f = %.6f\n\n", 
            k, p_treatment, p_control, denominator))

n_E <- m * k / denominator
n_C <- m / denominator

cat(sprintf("Sample sizes (continuous):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  n_E = m*k / (k*pE + pC) = %.6f * %.1f / %.6f = %.6f\n", 
            m, k, denominator, n_E))
cat(sprintf("  n_C = m / (k*pE + pC) = %.6f / %.6f = %.6f\n\n", 
            m, denominator, n_C))

# Round up to integers
n_E_int <- ceiling(n_E)
n_C_int <- ceiling(n_C)

cat(sprintf("Sample sizes (rounded up to integers):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  n_E = %d (from %.6f)\n", n_E_int, n_E))
cat(sprintf("  n_C = %d (from %.6f)\n", n_C_int, n_C))
cat(sprintf("  Total: %d\n\n", n_E_int + n_C_int))

# Compare with ssizeCT.default result
library(powerSurvEpi)
result_ssizeCT <- ssizeCT.default(
  power = power,
  k = k,
  pE = p_treatment,
  pC = p_control,
  RR = hr,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat(sprintf("=== Comparison with ssizeCT.default ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Manual calculation: n_E = %.6f → %d, n_C = %.6f → %d\n", 
            n_E, n_E_int, n_C, n_C_int))
cat(sprintf("  ssizeCT.default:    n_E = %d, n_C = %d\n", 
            result_ssizeCT[1], result_ssizeCT[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Match: %s\n", 
            if (n_E_int == result_ssizeCT[1] & n_C_int == result_ssizeCT[2]) "✓ YES" else "✗ NO"))

# Summary for structured reporting
cat(sprintf("\n=== Summary ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Method: Freedman approximation (1982) for log-rank test\n"))
cat(sprintf("Study design: Two-sided log-rank test\n"))
cat(sprintf("Hypothesis: H0: HR = 1 vs H1: HR ≠ 1\n"))
cat(sprintf("Significance level: %.4f (two-sided)\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Target power: %.2f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (HR): %.1f\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (treatment): %.4f\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (control): %.4f\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("Allocation ratio: %.1f:1\n\n", k))
cat(sprintf("PRIMARY RESULT:\n"))
cat(sprintf("Sample size per group: %d participants\n", n_E_int))
cat(sprintf("Total sample size: %d participants\n", n_E_int + n_C_int))

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).
